# Test cases: OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0

These test cases describe what must work for a customer of the shop.
Each file holds one test case with these parts:

- ID and title
- preconditions
- test data
- steps, with one expected result for each step

## Test environment

- The app is OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0 at `http://localhost:3000`.
- The app runs in quiet mode (`NODE_ENV=quiet`). Quiet mode turns off the welcome banner, the challenge notifications and the hints.
- The app creates a new database at each start.
- The cookie banner shows on the first visit. The cookie `cookieconsent_status=dismiss` hides it.
- The UI language is English.
- The app shows prices with the sign `¤`.

## Test data rules

- Each test case uses a new customer account. Register the account before the test. Each account has a unique email.
- The account is a normal customer account, not a deluxe account. A deluxe account gets other prices and no purchase limit.
- A test case must not use data from another test case.
- Product names and prices come from the shop catalog of v20.3.0.

## Saved address and saved card

Some test cases need a saved address or a saved card. Create them before the test with these values.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Address: `Country` | `Ukraine` |
| Address: `Name` | `Test Customer` |
| Address: `Mobile Number` | `501234567` |
| Address: `ZIP Code` | `01001` |
| Address: `Address` | `1 Khreshchatyk Street` |
| Address: `City` | `Kyiv` |
| Address: `State` | `Kyiv` |
| Card: `Name` | `Test Customer` |
| Card: `Card Number` | `4111111111111111` |
| Card: `Expiry Month` | `12` |
| Card: `Expiry Year` | `2090` |

## Coupon codes

The shop accepts a coupon only in the month that the coupon names.
A coupon code is the Z85 encoding (ZeroMQ RFC 32) of the text `<MMM><YY>-<NN>`:

- `<MMM>` is the month in capital letters: `JAN`, `FEB`, `MAR`, `APR`, `MAY`, `JUN`, `JUL`, `AUG`, `SEP`, `OCT`, `NOV`, `DEC`.
- `<YY>` is the last two digits of the year.
- `<NN>` is the discount in percent, with two digits.

Calculate the code when the test runs. Use the date of the machine that runs the app.
The npm package `z85` does the encoding: `z85.encode('OCT26-10')`.

Examples for October 2026:

| Text | Code | Meaning in October 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| `OCT26-10` | `pEw8phz3Tq` | valid coupon, 10% discount |
| `SEP26-10` | `q:<Irhz3Tq` | expired coupon, it names the previous month |

## Test cases

| ID | Title |
|---|---|
| TC-01 | Login with a valid and an invalid password |
| TC-02 | Add a product to the basket |
| TC-03 | Change the quantity and remove a product in the basket |
| TC-04 | Purchase limit for one product |
| TC-05 | Valid coupon on the payment step |
| TC-06 | Invalid coupon and expired coupon |
| TC-07 | Order with a card, from basket to order history |
| TC-08 | Payment with the wallet |
# TC-01: Login with a valid and an invalid password

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-01 |
| Title | Login with a valid and an invalid password |
| Area | Login |

## Preconditions

1. A customer account exists. The test knows its email and its password.
2. Nobody is logged in to the shop in the browser.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Email | the email of the new account, for example `tc01-<unique>@example.test` |
| Password | the password of the new account, for example `Passw0rd!tc01` |
| Wrong password | the account password with one more character, for example `Passw0rd!tc01x` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the login page `/#/login`. | The page shows the title `Login`, the fields `Email` and `Password`, and the button `Log in`. |
| 2 | Type the email and the wrong password. Click `Log in`. | The page shows the error `Invalid email or password.` The login page stays open. |
| 3 | Open the account menu with the button `Account` in the top bar. | The menu shows the item `Login`. The menu does not show the email. |
| 4 | Close the menu. Type the email and the correct password. Click `Log in`. | The shop opens the product list `/#/search`. |
| 5 | Open the account menu with the button `Account`. | The menu shows the email of the account. The menu shows the item `Logout`. |
# TC-02: Add a product to the basket

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-02 |
| Title | Add a product to the basket |
| Area | Basket |

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The basket of the customer is empty.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the product list `/#/search`. | The list shows the product with its name, its price `8.99¤` and the button `Add to Basket`. The basket counter in the top bar shows `0`. |
| 2 | Click `Add to Basket` on the product. | A message shows `Placed Eggfruit Juice (500ml) into basket.` The basket counter shows `1`. |
| 3 | Open the basket with the button `Your Basket` in the top bar. | The basket page `/#/basket` shows one row: `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, quantity `1`, price `8.99¤`. |
| 4 | Read the total of the basket. | The basket shows `Total Price: 8.99¤`. |
# TC-03: Change the quantity and remove a product in the basket

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-03 |
| Title | Change the quantity and remove a product in the basket |
| Area | Basket |

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The basket holds product A with quantity 1 and product B with quantity 1. No other products are in the basket.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product A | `Raspberry Juice (1000ml)`, price `4.99¤` |
| Product B | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤` |

In each step, the basket total is the sum of price × quantity for all rows.

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. | The basket shows product A with quantity `1` and product B with quantity `1`. The basket shows `Total Price: 13.98¤`. The basket counter shows `2`. |
| 2 | Click the plus button in the row of product A. | Product A has quantity `2`. The basket shows `Total Price: 18.97¤`. The basket counter shows `3`. |
| 3 | Click the minus button in the row of product A. | Product A has quantity `1`. The basket shows `Total Price: 13.98¤`. The basket counter shows `2`. |
| 4 | Click the minus button in the row of product A again. | Product A keeps quantity `1`. The row of product A stays in the basket. The basket shows `Total Price: 13.98¤`. |
| 5 | Click the trash button in the row of product A. | The basket has no row for product A. The row of product B stays with quantity `1`. The basket shows `Total Price: 8.99¤`. The basket counter shows `1`. |
# TC-04: Purchase limit for one product

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-04 |
| Title | Purchase limit for one product |
| Area | Basket |

Some products have a limit: one basket can hold only a set number of items of the product.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists. It is a normal customer account, not a deluxe account.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The basket of the customer is empty.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Apple Juice (1000ml)`, price `1.99¤` |
| Limit | 5 items in one basket |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the product list `/#/search`. Click `Add to Basket` on the product. | A message shows `Placed Apple Juice (1000ml) into basket.` The basket counter shows `1`. |
| 2 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click the plus button in the row of the product until the quantity is `5`. | The product has quantity `5`. The basket shows `Total Price: 9.95¤`. No error message shows. |
| 3 | Click the plus button in the row of the product one more time. | An error message shows `You can order only up to 5 items of this product.` |
| 4 | Read the basket. | The product keeps quantity `5`. The basket shows `Total Price: 9.95¤`. The basket counter shows `5`. |
| 5 | Open the product list `/#/search`. Click `Add to Basket` on the product. | An error message shows `You can order only up to 5 items of this product.` The basket counter shows `5`. |
# TC-05: Valid coupon on the payment step

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-05 |
| Title | Valid coupon on the payment step |
| Area | Coupon |

The discount of a coupon applies to the price of the products only. The delivery price does not get the discount.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
4. The basket holds the product with quantity 2. No other products are in the basket.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤`, quantity 2 |
| Delivery | `One Day Delivery`, price `0.99¤` |
| Coupon | the 10% coupon of the current month, see `README.md` |

Expected order summary:

| Line | Calculation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Items` | 2 × 8.99 | `17.98¤` |
| `Delivery` | price of `One Day Delivery` | `0.99¤` |
| `Promotion` | 10% of `Items` | `1.80¤` |
| `Total Price` | `Items` − `Promotion` + `Delivery` | `17.17¤` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click `Checkout`. | The page `Select an address` shows the saved address. |
| 2 | Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` shows `One Day Delivery` with price `0.99¤`, `Fast Delivery` with `0.50¤` and `Standard Delivery` with `0.00¤`. |
| 3 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` shows the saved card and the panel `Add a coupon`. |
| 4 | Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the coupon code in the field `Coupon`. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.` |
| 5 | Select the saved card. Click `Continue`. | The page `Order Summary` shows `Items` `17.98¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `1.80¤` and `Total Price` `17.17¤`. |
# TC-06: Invalid coupon and expired coupon

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-06 |
| Title | Invalid coupon and expired coupon |
| Area | Coupon |

The shop must not give a discount for a code that is not a coupon. The shop must not give a discount for a coupon of a past month.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
4. The basket holds the product with quantity 2. No other products are in the basket.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤`, quantity 2 |
| Delivery | `One Day Delivery`, price `0.99¤` |
| Invalid code | `abcdefghij`, 10 characters, not a coupon |
| Expired coupon | the 10% coupon of the previous month, see `README.md` |

Expected order summary, without a discount:

| Line | Value |
|---|---|
| `Items` | `17.98¤` |
| `Delivery` | `0.99¤` |
| `Promotion` | `0.00¤` |
| `Total Price` | `18.97¤` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` opens. |
| 2 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` opens. |
| 3 | Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the invalid code in the field `Coupon`. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows the error `Invalid coupon.` The page does not show `Your discount of`. |
| 4 | Type the expired coupon in the field `Coupon`. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows the error `Invalid coupon.` The page does not show `Your discount of`. |
| 5 | Select the saved card. Click `Continue`. | The page `Order Summary` shows `Items` `17.98¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `0.00¤` and `Total Price` `18.97¤`. |
# TC-07: Order with a card, from basket to order history

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-07 |
| Title | Order with a card, from basket to order history |
| Area | Checkout |

The basket page and the order summary calculate the totals in the browser.
The shop server calculates the total again when it saves the order.
The order confirmation page and the order history show the total that the server saved.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
4. The basket of the customer is empty.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product A | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤`, quantity 2 |
| Product B | `Carrot Juice (1000ml)`, price `2.99¤`, quantity 1 |
| Delivery | `One Day Delivery`, price `0.99¤` |
| Coupon | the 10% coupon of the current month, see `README.md` |

Expected totals:

| Line | Calculation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Items` | 2 × 8.99 + 1 × 2.99 | `20.97¤` |
| `Delivery` | price of `One Day Delivery` | `0.99¤` |
| `Promotion` | 10% of `Items` | `2.10¤` |
| `Total Price` | `Items` − `Promotion` + `Delivery` | `19.86¤` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the product list `/#/search`. Click `Add to Basket` on product A two times. Click `Add to Basket` on product B one time. | The basket counter shows `3`. |
| 2 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. | The basket shows product A with quantity `2` and product B with quantity `1`. The basket shows `Total Price: 20.97¤`. |
| 3 | Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` opens. |
| 4 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` opens. |
| 5 | Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the coupon code. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.` |
| 6 | Select the saved card. Click `Continue`. | The page `Order Summary` shows the saved address, the card, `Items` `20.97¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `2.10¤` and `Total Price` `19.86¤`. |
| 7 | Click `Place your order and pay`. | The confirmation page `/#/order-completion/<order ID>` shows `Thank you for your purchase!` |
| 8 | Read the order summary on the confirmation page. | It shows product A with quantity `2`, product B with quantity `1`, `Items` `20.97¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `2.10¤` and `Total Price` `19.86¤`. |
| 9 | Read the basket counter. Open the basket `/#/basket`. | The basket counter shows `0`. The basket has no products. The button `Checkout` is disabled. |
| 10 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Order History`. | The page `Order History` shows one order with the order ID from step 7 and `Total Price` `19.86¤`. The order shows product A with quantity `2` and product B with quantity `1`. |
# TC-08: Payment with the wallet

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-08 |
| Title | Payment with the wallet |
| Area | Wallet |

The customer can pay an order with the money in the wallet.
The wallet must hold at least the order total.
After each order, the shop adds the bonus points of the order to the wallet: 1 point = `1.00¤`.
The bonus points of one product are the product price divided by 10, rounded to a whole number, × quantity.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
   The shop adds money to the wallet only with a saved card.
4. The basket holds the product with quantity 1. No other products are in the basket.
5. The wallet balance is `5.00¤`. To get this balance, add `5` to the wallet of the new account with the saved card. A new account has the balance `0.00¤`.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤`, quantity 1 |
| Delivery | `Standard Delivery`, price `0.00¤` |
| Order total | `8.99¤` |
| First balance | `5.00¤`, less than the order total |
| Top-up for part 2 | `3.99¤`, so that the balance is exactly the order total |
| Bonus points of the order | round(8.99 / 10) × 1 = `1` |

## Steps

Part 1: the wallet holds less than the order total.

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` opens. |
| 2 | Select `Standard Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` shows `Wallet Balance` `5.00` and the button `Pay 8.99¤`. |
| 3 | Read the button `Pay 8.99¤`. | The button is disabled. The customer cannot pay with the wallet. |
| 4 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Order History`. | The page shows `You have not placed any orders yet.` |
| 5 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Digital Wallet`. | The wallet balance is `5.00`. |

Part 2: the wallet holds exactly the order total. Before step 6, add `3.99` to the wallet with the saved card. The balance is then `8.99¤`.

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. Select `Standard Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` shows `Wallet Balance` `8.99` and the button `Pay 8.99¤`. The button is enabled. |
| 7 | Click `Pay 8.99¤`. | The page `Order Summary` shows the payment method `Digital Wallet` and `Total Price` `8.99¤`. |
| 8 | Click `Place your order and pay`. | The confirmation page shows `Thank you for your purchase!` |
| 9 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Digital Wallet`. | The wallet balance is `1.00`: 8.99 − 8.99 + 1 bonus point. |
| 10 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Order History`. | The page shows one order with `Total Price` `8.99¤` and `Bonus` `1`. |

| 3 | Open the account menu with the button `Account` in the top bar. | The menu shows the item `Login`. The menu does not show the email. |
| 4 | Close the menu. Type the email and the correct password. Click `Log in`. | The shop opens the product list `/#/search`. |
| 5 | Open the account menu with the button `Account`. | The menu shows the email of the account. The menu shows the item `Logout`. |
# TC-02: Add a product to the basket

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-02 |
| Title | Add a product to the basket |
| Area | Basket |

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The basket of the customer is empty.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the product list `/#/search`. | The list shows the product with its name, its price `8.99¤` and the button `Add to Basket`. The basket counter in the top bar shows `0`. |
| 2 | Click `Add to Basket` on the product. | A message shows `Placed Eggfruit Juice (500ml) into basket.` The basket counter shows `1`. |
| 3 | Open the basket with the button `Your Basket` in the top bar. | The basket page `/#/basket` shows one row: `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, quantity `1`, price `8.99¤`. |
| 4 | Read the total of the basket. | The basket shows `Total Price: 8.99¤`. |
# TC-03: Change the quantity and remove a product in the basket

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-03 |
| Title | Change the quantity and remove a product in the basket |
| Area | Basket |

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The basket holds product A with quantity 1 and product B with quantity 1. No other products are in the basket.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product A | `Raspberry Juice (1000ml)`, price `4.99¤` |
| Product B | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤` |

In each step, the basket total is the sum of price × quantity for all rows.

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. | The basket shows product A with quantity `1` and product B with quantity `1`. The basket shows `Total Price: 13.98¤`. The basket counter shows `2`. |
| 2 | Click the plus button in the row of product A. | Product A has quantity `2`. The basket shows `Total Price: 18.97¤`. The basket counter shows `3`. |
| 3 | Click the minus button in the row of product A. | Product A has quantity `1`. The basket shows `Total Price: 13.98¤`. The basket counter shows `2`. |
| 4 | Click the minus button in the row of product A again. | Product A keeps quantity `1`. The row of product A stays in the basket. The basket shows `Total Price: 13.98¤`. |
| 5 | Click the trash button in the row of product A. | The basket has no row for product A. The row of product B stays with quantity `1`. The basket shows `Total Price: 8.99¤`. The basket counter shows `1`. |
# TC-04: Purchase limit for one product

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-04 |
| Title | Purchase limit for one product |
| Area | Basket |

Some products have a limit: one basket can hold only a set number of items of the product.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists. It is a normal customer account, not a deluxe account.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The basket of the customer is empty.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Apple Juice (1000ml)`, price `1.99¤` |
| Limit | 5 items in one basket |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the product list `/#/search`. Click `Add to Basket` on the product. | A message shows `Placed Apple Juice (1000ml) into basket.` The basket counter shows `1`. |
| 2 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click the plus button in the row of the product until the quantity is `5`. | The product has quantity `5`. The basket shows `Total Price: 9.95¤`. No error message shows. |
| 3 | Click the plus button in the row of the product one more time. | An error message shows `You can order only up to 5 items of this product.` |
| 4 | Read the basket. | The product keeps quantity `5`. The basket shows `Total Price: 9.95¤`. The basket counter shows `5`. |
| 5 | Open the product list `/#/search`. Click `Add to Basket` on the product. | An error message shows `You can order only up to 5 items of this product.` The basket counter shows `5`. |
# TC-05: Valid coupon on the payment step

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-05 |
| Title | Valid coupon on the payment step |
| Area | Coupon |

The discount of a coupon applies to the price of the products only. The delivery price does not get the discount.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
4. The basket holds the product with quantity 2. No other products are in the basket.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤`, quantity 2 |
| Delivery | `One Day Delivery`, price `0.99¤` |
| Coupon | the 10% coupon of the current month, see `README.md` |

Expected order summary:

| Line | Calculation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Items` | 2 × 8.99 | `17.98¤` |
| `Delivery` | price of `One Day Delivery` | `0.99¤` |
| `Promotion` | 10% of `Items` | `1.80¤` |
| `Total Price` | `Items` − `Promotion` + `Delivery` | `17.17¤` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click `Checkout`. | The page `Select an address` shows the saved address. |
| 2 | Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` shows `One Day Delivery` with price `0.99¤`, `Fast Delivery` with `0.50¤` and `Standard Delivery` with `0.00¤`. |
| 3 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` shows the saved card and the panel `Add a coupon`. |
| 4 | Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the coupon code in the field `Coupon`. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.` |
| 5 | Select the saved card. Click `Continue`. | The page `Order Summary` shows `Items` `17.98¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `1.80¤` and `Total Price` `17.17¤`. |
# TC-06: Invalid coupon and expired coupon

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-06 |
| Title | Invalid coupon and expired coupon |
| Area | Coupon |

The shop must not give a discount for a code that is not a coupon. The shop must not give a discount for a coupon of a past month.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
4. The basket holds the product with quantity 2. No other products are in the basket.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤`, quantity 2 |
| Delivery | `One Day Delivery`, price `0.99¤` |
| Invalid code | `abcdefghij`, 10 characters, not a coupon |
| Expired coupon | the 10% coupon of the previous month, see `README.md` |

Expected order summary, without a discount:

| Line | Value |
|---|---|
| `Items` | `17.98¤` |
| `Delivery` | `0.99¤` |
| `Promotion` | `0.00¤` |
| `Total Price` | `18.97¤` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` opens. |
| 2 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` opens. |
| 3 | Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the invalid code in the field `Coupon`. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows the error `Invalid coupon.` The page does not show `Your discount of`. |
| 4 | Type the expired coupon in the field `Coupon`. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows the error `Invalid coupon.` The page does not show `Your discount of`. |
| 5 | Select the saved card. Click `Continue`. | The page `Order Summary` shows `Items` `17.98¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `0.00¤` and `Total Price` `18.97¤`. |
# TC-07: Order with a card, from basket to order history

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-07 |
| Title | Order with a card, from basket to order history |
| Area | Checkout |

The basket page and the order summary calculate the totals in the browser.
The shop server calculates the total again when it saves the order.
The order confirmation page and the order history show the total that the server saved.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
4. The basket of the customer is empty.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product A | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤`, quantity 2 |
| Product B | `Carrot Juice (1000ml)`, price `2.99¤`, quantity 1 |
| Delivery | `One Day Delivery`, price `0.99¤` |
| Coupon | the 10% coupon of the current month, see `README.md` |

Expected totals:

| Line | Calculation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Items` | 2 × 8.99 + 1 × 2.99 | `20.97¤` |
| `Delivery` | price of `One Day Delivery` | `0.99¤` |
| `Promotion` | 10% of `Items` | `2.10¤` |
| `Total Price` | `Items` − `Promotion` + `Delivery` | `19.86¤` |

## Steps

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the product list `/#/search`. Click `Add to Basket` on product A two times. Click `Add to Basket` on product B one time. | The basket counter shows `3`. |
| 2 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. | The basket shows product A with quantity `2` and product B with quantity `1`. The basket shows `Total Price: 20.97¤`. |
| 3 | Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` opens. |
| 4 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` opens. |
| 5 | Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the coupon code. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.` |
| 6 | Select the saved card. Click `Continue`. | The page `Order Summary` shows the saved address, the card, `Items` `20.97¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `2.10¤` and `Total Price` `19.86¤`. |
| 7 | Click `Place your order and pay`. | The confirmation page `/#/order-completion/<order ID>` shows `Thank you for your purchase!` |
| 8 | Read the order summary on the confirmation page. | It shows product A with quantity `2`, product B with quantity `1`, `Items` `20.97¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `2.10¤` and `Total Price` `19.86¤`. |
| 9 | Read the basket counter. Open the basket `/#/basket`. | The basket counter shows `0`. The basket has no products. The button `Checkout` is disabled. |
| 10 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Order History`. | The page `Order History` shows one order with the order ID from step 7 and `Total Price` `19.86¤`. The order shows product A with quantity `2` and product B with quantity `1`. |
# TC-08: Payment with the wallet

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | TC-08 |
| Title | Payment with the wallet |
| Area | Wallet |

The customer can pay an order with the money in the wallet.
The wallet must hold at least the order total.
After each order, the shop adds the bonus points of the order to the wallet: 1 point = `1.00¤`.
The bonus points of one product are the product price divided by 10, rounded to a whole number, × quantity.

## Preconditions

1. A new customer account exists.
2. The customer is logged in.
3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
   The shop adds money to the wallet only with a saved card.
4. The basket holds the product with quantity 1. No other products are in the basket.
5. The wallet balance is `5.00¤`. To get this balance, add `5` to the wallet of the new account with the saved card. A new account has the balance `0.00¤`.

## Test data

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, price `8.99¤`, quantity 1 |
| Delivery | `Standard Delivery`, price `0.00¤` |
| Order total | `8.99¤` |
| First balance | `5.00¤`, less than the order total |
| Top-up for part 2 | `3.99¤`, so that the balance is exactly the order total |
| Bonus points of the order | round(8.99 / 10) × 1 = `1` |

## Steps

Part 1: the wallet holds less than the order total.

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` opens. |
| 2 | Select `Standard Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` shows `Wallet Balance` `5.00` and the button `Pay 8.99¤`. |
| 3 | Read the button `Pay 8.99¤`. | The button is disabled. The customer cannot pay with the wallet. |
| 4 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Order History`. | The page shows `You have not placed any orders yet.` |
| 5 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Digital Wallet`. | The wallet balance is `5.00`. |

Part 2: the wallet holds exactly the order total. Before step 6, add `3.99` to the wallet with the saved card. The balance is then `8.99¤`.

| # | Step | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. Select `Standard Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` shows `Wallet Balance` `8.99` and the button `Pay 8.99¤`. The button is enabled. |
| 7 | Click `Pay 8.99¤`. | The page `Order Summary` shows the payment method `Digital Wallet` and `Total Price` `8.99¤`. |
| 8 | Click `Place your order and pay`. | The confirmation page shows `Thank you for your purchase!` |
| 9 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Digital Wallet`. | The wallet balance is `1.00`: 8.99 − 8.99 + 1 bonus point. |
| 10 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Order History`. | The page shows one order with `Total Price` `8.99¤` and `Bonus` `1`. |

6	import { Component, NgZone, type OnInit, inject, ChangeDetectionStrategy } from '@angular/core'
7	import { DeliveryService } from '../Services/delivery.service'
8	import { AddressService } from '../Services/address.service'

10	import { Router } from '@angular/router'
11	import { Location, NgClass } from '@angular/common'
12	import { type DeliveryMethod } from '../Models/deliveryMethod.model'
13	import { library } from '@fortawesome/fontawesome-svg-core'
14	import { faRocket, faShippingFast, faTruck } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
15	import { SelectionModel } from '@angular/cdk/collections'
16	import { MatIconModule } from '@angular/material/icon'
17	import { MatButtonModule } from '@angular/material/button'
18	
19	import { MatRadioButton } from '@angular/material/radio'
20	
21	import { MatDivider } from '@angular/material/divider'
22	import { TranslateModule } from '@ngx-translate/core'
23	import { MatCardModule } from '@angular/material/card'
24	
25	library.add(faRocket, faShippingFast, faTruck)
26	
27	@Component({
28	  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager,
29	  selector: 'app-delivery-method',
30	  templateUrl: './delivery-method.component.html',
31	  styleUrls: ['./delivery-method.component.scss'],
32	  imports: [MatCardModule, TranslateModule, MatDivider, MatTable, MatColumnDef, MatHeaderCellDef, MatHeaderCell, MatCellDef, MatCell, MatRadioButton, NgClass, MatHeaderRowDef, MatHeaderRow, MatRowDef, MatRow, MatButtonModule, MatIconModule]
33	})
34	export class DeliveryMethodComponent implements OnInit {
35	  private readonly location = inject(Location)
36	  private readonly deliverySerivce = inject(DeliveryService)
37	  private readonly addressService = inject(AddressService)
38	  private readonly router = inject(Router)
39	  private readonly ngZone = inject(NgZone)
40	
41	  public displayedColumns = ['Selection', 'Name', 'Price', 'ETA']
42	  public methods: DeliveryMethod[]
43	  public address: any
44	  public dataSource
45	  public deliveryMethodId: number = undefined
46	  selection = new SelectionModel<DeliveryMethod>(false, [])
47	
48	  ngOnInit (): void {
49	    this.addressService.getById(sessionStorage.getItem('addressId')).subscribe({
50	      next: (address) => {
51	        this.address = address
52	      },
53	      error: (error) => { console.log(error) }
54	    })
55	
56	    this.deliverySerivce.get().subscribe({
57	      next: (methods) => {
58	        this.methods = methods
59	        this.dataSource = new MatTableDataSource<DeliveryMethod>(this.methods)
60	      },
61	      error: (error) => { console.log(error) }
62	    })
63	  }
64	
65	  selectMethod (id) {
66	    if (this.selection.hasValue() || id) {
67	      this.deliveryMethodId = id
68	    } else {
69	      this.deliveryMethodId = undefined
70	    }
71	  }
72	
73	  routeToPreviousUrl () {
74	    this.location.back()
75	  }
76	
77	  chooseDeliveryMethod () {
78	    sessionStorage.setItem('deliveryMethodId', this.deliveryMethodId.toString())
79	    this.ngZone.run(async () => await this.router.navigate(['/payment', 'shop']))
80	  }
81	}

6	import { Component, NgZone, inject, ChangeDetectionStrategy } from '@angular/core'

8	import { faCartArrowDown } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
9	import { Router } from '@angular/router'

17	@Component({
18	  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager,
19	  selector: 'app-basket',
20	  templateUrl: './basket.component.html',
21	  styleUrls: ['./basket.component.scss'],
22	  imports: [MatCardModule, PurchaseBasketComponent, MatButtonModule, TranslateModule]
23	})
24	export class BasketComponent {
25	  private readonly router = inject(Router)
26	  private readonly ngZone = inject(NgZone)
27	
28	  public productCount = 0
29	  public bonus = 0
30	
31	  checkout (): void {
32	    if (localStorage.getItem('token') == null) {
33	      this.ngZone.run(async () => await this.router.navigate(['/login'], {
34	        queryParams: {
35	          redirectUrl: '/basket'
36	        }
37	      }))
38	      return
39	    }
40	
41	    this.ngZone.run(async () => await this.router.navigate(['/address/select']))
42	  }
43	
44	  getProductCount (total: number): void {
45	    this.productCount = total
46	  }
47	
48	  getBonusPoints (total: [number, number]): void {
49	    sessionStorage.setItem('itemTotal', total[0].toString())
50	    this.bonus = total[1]
51	  }
52	}

# UI patches for OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0

This folder holds 4 UI patches. Each patch is one UI change that a product team can release.
The patches change only files under `frontend/src/`.
They do not change the server, the API, the database, the products or the prices.

| File | Kind | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `01-rename-add-to-basket-button.patch` | 1. Rename a button | `Add to Basket` becomes `Add to Cart` |
| `02-login-form-layout.patch` | 2. Change the structure of a form | The login form gets a new field label and a new order of its parts |
| `03-move-coupon-to-basket.patch` | 3. Move a step of the checkout | The coupon panel moves from `My Payment Options` to the basket page |
| `04-rename-place-order-button.patch` | 1. Rename a button | `Place your order and pay` becomes `Confirm and pay` |

## 01: rename the button `Add to Basket`

Kind: 1, rename a button.

File: `frontend/src/assets/i18n/en.json`, key `ADD_BASKET`.

What changes for a user:

- On each product card in the product list `/#/search`, the button shows `Add to Cart`. Before the change, it showed `Add to Basket`.
- The product detail dialog uses the same key. Its button also shows `Add to Cart`.
- The button has the same position, the same icon and the same function.
- The message after the click does not change: `Placed <product> into basket.`
- The top bar button `Your Basket` does not change.

Test case steps that the change touches:

| Test case | Step | How a person does the step after the change |
|---|---|---|
| TC-02 | 1 | The product card shows the name, the price `8.99¤` and the button `Add to Cart`. |
| TC-02 | 2 | Click `Add to Cart` on the product. |
| TC-04 | 1, 5 | Click `Add to Cart` on the product. |
| TC-07 | 1 | Click `Add to Cart` on product A two times and on product B one time. |

## 02: change the structure of the login form

Kind: 2, change the structure of a form.

Files: `frontend/src/app/login/login.component.html`, `frontend/src/app/login/login.component.scss`, `frontend/src/assets/i18n/en.json` (new key `LABEL_EMAIL_ADDRESS`).

What changes for a user on the login page `/#/login`:

- The label of the email field is `Email address`. Before the change, it was `Email`.
- The checkbox `Remember me` moves up. It is now below the field `Password` and above the button `Log in`. Before the change, it was below the button.
- The link `Forgot your password?` moves down. It is now below the button `Log in`, in the center. Before the change, it was below the field `Password`.
- The title `Login`, the field `Password`, the button `Log in` and the error `Invalid email or password.` do not change.
- The registration page and the page "forgot password" keep the label `Email`.

Test case steps that the change touches:

| Test case | Step | How a person does the step after the change |
|---|---|---|
| TC-01 | 1 | The page shows the title `Login`, the fields `Email address` and `Password`, and the button `Log in`. |
| TC-01 | 2, 4 | Type the email in the field `Email address`. Type the password in the field `Password`. Click `Log in`. The checkbox `Remember me` is now between the field `Password` and the button `Log in`. Do not click it. |

The login of the other test cases (TC-02 to TC-08, precondition "the customer is logged in") also uses this form if a person logs in through the UI.

## 03: move the coupon to the basket page

Kind: 3, move a step of the checkout.

Files: `frontend/src/app/basket/basket.component.html`, `.ts`, `.scss`, `frontend/src/app/payment/payment.component.html`, `.ts`.

What changes for a user:

- The basket page `/#/basket` shows the panel `Add a coupon`. The panel is below the product list and above the button `Checkout`.
- The page `My Payment Options` does not show the panel `Add a coupon`. The page still shows the saved cards, `Wallet Balance`, the button `Pay <total>¤` and the panel `Other payment options`.
- The panel holds the same parts as before: the field `Coupon`, the button `Redeem` and the same messages.
- The coupon logic does not change. It is the same code and calls the same API. The discount, the message `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.` and the error `Invalid coupon.` do not change.
- The basket line `Total Price` shows the price without the discount, as before. The order summary shows the line `Promotion` and the discounted `Total Price`, as before. The button `Pay <total>¤` on the page `My Payment Options` includes the discount, as before.

Test case steps that the change touches:

| Test case | Step | How a person does the step after the change |
|---|---|---|
| TC-05 | 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the coupon code in the field `Coupon`. Click `Redeem`. The basket shows `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.` Then click `Checkout`. The page `Select an address` shows the saved address. |
| TC-05 | 2 | No change. |
| TC-05 | 3 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. The page `My Payment Options` shows the saved card. It does not show the panel `Add a coupon`. |
| TC-05 | 4 | The person did this step in the basket, before the click on `Checkout` (see step 1). |
| TC-05 | 5 | No change. The page `Order Summary` shows `Items` `17.98¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `1.80¤` and `Total Price` `17.17¤`. |
| TC-06 | 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Do steps 3 and 4 here: type the invalid code, click `Redeem`, read the error `Invalid coupon.`. Then type the expired coupon, click `Redeem`, read the error `Invalid coupon.`. Then click `Checkout`, select the saved address and click `Continue`. |
| TC-06 | 2 | No change. The page `My Payment Options` opens, without the panel `Add a coupon`. |
| TC-06 | 3, 4 | The person did these steps in the basket (see step 1). |
| TC-06 | 5 | No change. `Promotion` is `0.00¤` and `Total Price` is `18.97¤`. |
| TC-07 | 2 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Do step 5 here: open the panel `Add a coupon`, type the coupon code, click `Redeem`, read `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.`. |
| TC-07 | 3, 4 | No change. Click `Checkout` in the basket. |
| TC-07 | 5 | The person did this step in the basket (see step 2). |
| TC-07 | 6 | No change. `Promotion` is `2.10¤` and `Total Price` is `19.86¤`. |

TC-08 does not use a coupon. Its steps on the page `My Payment Options` (`Wallet Balance`, the button `Pay 8.99¤`) do not change.

## 04: rename the button `Place your order and pay`

Kind: 1, rename a button.

File: `frontend/src/assets/i18n/en.json`, key `PLACE_ORDER_AND_PAY`.

What changes for a user:

- On the page `Order Summary`, the button shows `Confirm and pay`. Before the change, it showed `Place your order and pay`.
- The button has the same position and the same function. The confirmation page `Thank you for your purchase!` does not change.

Test case steps that the change touches:

| Test case | Step | How a person does the step after the change |
|---|---|---|
| TC-07 | 7 | Click `Confirm and pay`. The confirmation page `/#/order-completion/<order ID>` shows `Thank you for your purchase!` |
| TC-08 | 8 | Click `Confirm and pay`. The confirmation page shows `Thank you for your purchase!` |

## All patches together

With all 4 patches, each change in the sections 01 to 04 applies. The changes do not have an effect on each other.
In TC-07, for example, a person clicks `Add to Cart` (01), logs in with the field `Email address` (02), redeems the coupon in the basket (03) and clicks `Confirm and pay` (04).

Steps that no patch touches: TC-01 steps 3 and 5, TC-02 steps 3 and 4, TC-03 all steps, TC-04 steps 2 to 4, TC-07 steps 8 to 10, TC-08 steps 1 to 7 and 9 to 10.

## Results of the checks

### `git apply --check`, each patch alone on v20.3.0

Command: `git -C ../juice-shop apply --check ../sealed-ui/<file>.patch`. Before each command, `../juice-shop` was at the tag v20.3.0 with no changes.

```
01 alone: exit 0
02 alone: exit 0
03 alone: exit 0
04 alone: exit 0
```

### All patches together, in file-name order

For each patch in the order 01, 02, 03, 04: `git apply --check`, then `git apply`, on top of the patches before it.

```
01: check exit 0, applied
02 on top of 01: check exit 0, applied
03 on top of 01-02: check exit 0, applied
04 on top of 01-03: check exit 0, applied
```

`git -C ../juice-shop status --porcelain` after all 4 patches:

```
 M frontend/src/app/basket/basket.component.html
 M frontend/src/app/basket/basket.component.scss
 M frontend/src/app/basket/basket.component.ts
 M frontend/src/app/login/login.component.html
 M frontend/src/app/login/login.component.scss
 M frontend/src/app/payment/payment.component.html
 M frontend/src/app/payment/payment.component.ts
 M frontend/src/assets/i18n/en.json
```

### Build with all patches

Command, in `../juice-shop/frontend`:

```
npx ng build --configuration production --output-path "$TMPDIR/ui-patch-build"
```

Result: the build passed, with no errors and no warnings in the output. Last lines of the output:

```
Application bundle generation complete. [11.283 seconds] - 2026-10-21T16:08:32.431Z

Output location: /var/folders/8v/tjlqcph57g934z54rbf7jfk40000gn/T/ui-patch-build
```

The build did not write into `../juice-shop/frontend/dist`. The app was not started.

### Reset of the app

After the build: `git -C ../juice-shop checkout -- .`.
Then `git -C ../juice-shop status --porcelain` gave no output, and `git -C ../juice-shop describe --tags --exact-match HEAD` gave `v20.3.0`.

## Limits

- Nobody did the steps of TC-01 to TC-08 in a browser with the patches. The analysis of the steps above comes from the source code. The build shows only that the code compiles.
- The unit tests of the frontend were not run or read. The task did not permit it. The unit tests of the basket, payment and login components can fail with patches 02 and 03.

# Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100)

ASD-STE100 is a controlled-language standard built by the aerospace and defense industry (ASD, the AeroSpace and Defense Industries Association of Europe) to stop maintenance technicians from misreading English instructions. The standard removes the two biggest sources of misreading: words with more than one meaning, and sentences with more than one possible structure.

This skill borrows that same discipline for a different reader: an **AI agent or a downstream system** that has to parse an English string — an error message, a tool description, an inter-agent instruction, a status report — without a human in the loop to resolve ambiguity. If a maintenance technician can misread "close the valve" as an adjective ("the valve that is near") instead of a command, so can a language model.

## When to Use This Skill

- An agent's output (explanation, instruction, log message, tool description) reads as dense, jargon-heavy, or ambiguous.
- Text will be consumed by another agent, a translation pipeline, or a non-native English reader, and misparsing has a real cost.
- You are writing a prompt, system message, or tool description and want to remove ambiguity before a model ever sees it.
- You want a **before/after** comparison showing exactly which rule was violated and how the rewrite fixes it. Ask for it — the default output is the rewritten text alone (see Output Format).

This skill is not for creative or marketing copy — STE is deliberately flat and literal. Do not apply it to text where voice, nuance, or persuasion is the point.

## Two Modes

Pick a mode before rewriting. If the user does not say which, infer from the text type and state the choice in one line.

**Strict** — procedures, error messages, tool and function descriptions, inter-agent instructions, safety text. Anywhere a wrong reading has a cost. Apply every rule below, including the hard length caps and one-word-one-meaning discipline.

**STE-flavored** — READMEs, PR descriptions, changelogs, explanatory prose. Apply the structural rules in full and treat the lexical rules as advisory (see Core Rewrite Rules for that split). In practice that means keeping the sentence length caps, active voice, simple tenses, no phrasal verbs, no semicolons, no nominalization and no marketing adjectives, while dropping the one-word-one-meaning lockdown: prose needs some range, and a strict rewrite of prose reads as a personality transplant rather than a clarification.

The two modes and the structural/lexical split are the same distinction seen from two directions. The split says which rules this skill can verify without ASD's dictionary. The modes say which of them to enforce for a given kind of text.

## Source and Scope

This skill encodes the **rule categories** of ASD-STE100 Issue 9 (Jan 2025): 53 writing rules across 9 sections covering word choice, grammar, sentence structure, and style, backed by a dictionary of ~900 approved words (one meaning, one part of speech each) and ~1,200 words to avoid with suggested replacements. See `references/writing-rules.md` for the full rule summary and citations.

It does **not** reproduce ASD's ~900-word approved dictionary verbatim. ASD-STE100 is free to obtain, but it is not free to redistribute: Issue 9, page 2 states that "no reproduction or publication of it, in whole or in part, shall be made without the written authority of an officer of ASD," and grants free reproduction rights only to eight listed categories (ASD/AIA/AIAC member associations and their member companies and customers, member-state defence ministries, A4A, airworthiness authorities, and universities and research institutes for educational purposes). This project is in none of them, so the dictionary stays out of this repo.

Instead, this skill applies the *underlying principle* (pick the plainest, most common word available and use it the same way every time) rather than checking against a fixed word list. When exact ASD-approved wording matters (e.g. actual aircraft maintenance documentation), get the standard and check word-by-word against the real dictionary. Request it from the [official downloads page](https://www.asd-ste100.org/STE_downloads.html) — note that this is a request form that emails you a link, not a direct download.

## Core Rewrite Rules

STE's rules divide into two kinds, and this skill can only fully deliver one of them. **Structural rules** are self-contained: they describe sentence shape, and you can apply them from the description alone. **Lexical rules** are defined entirely by the official ~900-word dictionary, which this skill deliberately does not reproduce (see Source and Scope). Without that dictionary, the lexical rules degrade from a checkable standard into a preference for plain words.

Apply the structural rules with confidence. Apply the lexical rules as a direction of travel, and say so in your output rather than implying dictionary compliance you cannot verify.

### Structural rules — apply these

| Rule | Do | Don't |
|---|---|---|
| Active voice | "The agent deletes the file." | "The file is deleted (by the agent)." — unless the actor is genuinely unknown or irrelevant |
| No phrasal verbs (Rule 9.3) | "Remove the panel." / "Start the job." | "Take off the panel." / "Spin up the job." — a two-word verb has meanings the parts do not predict |
| One instruction per sentence | "Open the file. Read line 3." | "Open the file and read line 3, then check if it matches." |
| Sentence length | ≤20 words for instructions/procedures, ≤25 words for descriptions | Long compound/subordinate-clause sentences |
| No semicolons (Rule 8.1) | Split into separate sentences | Any semicolon at all — STE bans the mark outright, not only as a clause join. (Rule 8.1 permits every other standard punctuation mark. The em dash is *not* banned by STE, though it often signals a sentence that should be split.) |
| Noun clusters | ≤3 words stacked as a noun phrase ("fuel pump valve") | 4+ word noun stacks ("high pressure fuel pump inlet valve assembly") |
| No ellipsis | Keep the subject, verb, and article explicit even if it reads longer | Drop words to save space ("Files not backed up will be lost" → ambiguous which files) |
| Keep modality | "The request **may have** failed." stays "may have" | Promote a hedge to a fact ("The request failed.") or invent a certainty the source did not state |
| Paragraph limits | One topic per paragraph, ≤6 sentences | Multi-topic paragraphs |
| Lists for sequences | Use a numbered or bulleted list for 3+ steps or conditions | Bury a sequence inside one prose sentence |

### Lexical rules — direction of travel only

| Rule | Do | Don't | Why it is weaker here |
|---|---|---|---|
| One word, one meaning | Pick one verb for one action and reuse it every time (e.g. always "check", never mix "check"/"verify"/"confirm" for the same action) | Rotate synonyms for the same idea across a document | Consistency within a document is checkable. Which word is the *approved* one is not, without the dictionary. |
| One part of speech per word | "Apply oil to the valve" (oil = noun) | "Oil the valve" (oil = verb) | Whether "oil" is approved as a noun only is a dictionary fact. Prefer the noun form when both read equally well. Do not claim compliance. |
| Verb, not noun (Rule 3.7) | "Analyze the log." | "Perform an analysis of the log." — a noun form of an action makes the sentence longer and hides who acts | Rule 3.7 says "use an **approved** verb to describe an action." Preferring the verb form is safe to apply anywhere. Knowing which verb is the approved one needs the dictionary. |
| Domain terms | Keep necessary technical nouns/verbs, but define them once if not common English (STE allows a project-specific glossary beyond its base dictionary) | Use jargon without ever defining it | The glossary allowance is real STE, but the base dictionary it extends is absent. |

### Simple tenses — apply with one exception

STE permits infinitive, imperative, simple present, simple past, simple future, and past participle as adjective. It excludes present perfect and other compound forms: "we received the report", not "we have received the report".

Aircraft manuals never need present perfect, so the exclusion costs the standard nothing. Other text is not always so lucky. "The job has completed" (and its output is available now) and "the job completed" (at some past point) are different statements, and status text frequently needs the first. **Where the compound form carries information the simple form cannot — current relevance, or a hedge as in "may have failed" — keep it and flag the departure.** Elsewhere, follow the rule.

## Scan Checklist

These six habits cover most of what makes machine-written English hard to parse. Each one is mechanical: you can point at the exact word or punctuation mark that breaks the rule, with no judgment call. Scan for all six before you rewrite anything.

1. **Synonym rotation** — the same thing gets several names in one document ("the user", "the customer", "the client"). The reader cannot tell whether they are one thing or three. Fix: pick one name, use it every time.
2. **Hedge stacking** — helper verbs and qualifiers pile up until the sentence asserts nothing ("it is important to note that this may potentially help to improve"). Fix: state the claim, or delete it.
3. **Nominalization** — an action frozen into a noun ("perform an analysis of", "provides assistance to"). Fix: use the verb ("analyze", "helps").
4. **Marketing adjectives** — words that claim quality instead of showing it: seamless, robust, powerful, cutting-edge, effortless, blazing-fast. Fix: delete, or replace with the measurement that earns the claim.
5. **Run-on sentences** — several ideas joined by semicolons or em dashes. Fix: one idea per sentence.
6. **Soft phrasal verbs** — spin up, reach out, dive into, kick off. Fix: use the single plain verb (start, contact, read, begin).

## Process

1. Pick the mode (Strict or STE-flavored). Say which only when the user asked for the rule table — see Output Format.
2. Read the input text once for meaning — do not start rewriting before you understand what it must still say afterward.
3. Walk it sentence by sentence. Flag every rule violation from the Core Rewrite Rules tables and every habit from the Scan Checklist. In STE-flavored mode, flag the lexical rules but do not enforce them. For a mechanical first pass over the structural rules, run `scripts/ste-lint.py` (stdin or file args, `--json` for structured output); it checks semicolons, sentence length, phrasal verbs, nominalization, marketing adjectives, synonym rotation, dangling-conjunction in supported list items, passive voice, and compound tenses, and by design never flags hedges or modality. `--baseline N` tolerates N hard violations (for adopting on existing docs); `--disable rule1,rule2` silences named rules.
4. Rewrite each flagged sentence to fix the violation while preserving the original meaning exactly. If a rewrite would drop necessary precision (a safety condition, a scope qualifier, a number), keep the longer phrasing and flag it instead of silently simplifying.
   - **Check modality before you commit to a rewrite.** Hedges ("may", "could", "sometimes", "is likely to") carry the author's confidence, and confidence is content. A shorter sentence that upgrades a hedge to a fact is not a simplification — it is a different claim. This is the most common way a well-intentioned STE rewrite goes wrong, because hedges are exactly what a length cap tempts you to cut.
   - Never add a fact the source did not state. A rewrite that reads better because it supplies a cause, a frequency, or a mechanism has stopped being a rewrite.
5. Output the rewritten text (see Output Format). Keep the mode choice and the rule analysis internal unless the user asked to see them.
6. If the input already complies, say so — do not force changes onto compliant text.

## Output Format

**Default: the rewritten text, and nothing else.** Most callers want a result they can paste straight into a tool description, an error string, or a prompt. Print the simplified text on its own. Do not add a preamble about this skill, a mode announcement, a violation count, a summary of what changed, a rule table, or a closing offer to explain further.

The one permitted addition: if step 4 kept a longer phrasing on purpose, add a single line after the text, prefixed `Kept as-is:`, naming the phrase and the precision that would have been lost. Omit the line when there is nothing to report.

**On request: the rule table.** When the user asks to see the reasoning — "show the diff", "which rules did it break", "explain the changes", "before/after" — output this table instead:

```markdown
| Rule violated | Original | Simplified |
|---|---|---|
| Present perfect tense | "We have received your request." | "We received your request." |
| Noun cluster (4+ words) | "the agent task queue priority handler" | "the handler that sets task-queue priority" |

Mode: Strict. 7 violations found.
```

Follow the table with a one-line note on anything you deliberately did **not** simplify, and why (usually: simplifying would lose required precision).

## Boundaries

**Will:**
- Rewrite ambiguous or dense English into short, single-meaning, active-voice sentences.
- Return the rewritten text alone by default, and name the rules it applied when the user asks.
- Preserve every fact, condition, and scope qualifier in the original.
- Preserve the strength of every hedge, and add no claim the source did not make.
- Suggest a one-line glossary entry for domain terms that must stay.

**Will not:**
- Reproduce ASD's official ~900-word dictionary as if it were memorized verbatim — always treat the official download as the source of truth for exact approved wording.
- Simplify creative, marketing, or persuasive copy where voice and nuance are the point.
- Silently drop a safety condition, exception, or scope qualifier to shorten a sentence — it will flag the trade-off instead.
- Convert "may have failed" into "failed", or "could be caused by X" into "X is the cause" — losing a hedge changes the claim.
- Guarantee an aerospace/defense-grade STE-compliant document. This is a general-purpose clarity tool inspired by STE, not a certified STE authoring tool.
- Make weak content true or useful. STE fixes the *form* of a text, not its substance. A hollow paragraph rewritten under these rules becomes a clean, short, well-punctuated hollow paragraph. If the text has nothing to say, no rewrite fixes that — say so instead of polishing it.
- Shorten past the point of clarity. Cutting words is not the goal. Removing ambiguity is the goal. Past a certain point compression starts costing the reader time rather than saving it, so stop when the sentence is unambiguous, not when it is shortest.

## Additional Resources

- **`references/writing-rules.md`** — fuller summary of the 9 rule sections and dictionary structure, with citations to the official standard and secondary sources.
- **`examples/before-after.md`** — worked examples, including official STE examples and agent-output examples built for this skill.
- **`scripts/ste-lint.py`** — deterministic, stdlib-only linter for the structural rules, including dangling-conjunction in supported list items, plus a synonym-rotation check (one word, one meaning) scoped per file. Exit 1 when hard violations exceed `--baseline` (default 0); advisory findings (passive voice, compound tenses) never fail the run; `--disable` silences named rules. It never flags hedges or modality: those are content, not style, and `--selftest` asserts that "may have failed" passes clean.

# UI patches for OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0

This folder holds 4 UI patches. Each patch is one UI change that a product team can release.
The patches change only files under `frontend/src/`.
They do not change the server, the API, the database, the products or the prices.

| File | Kind | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `01-rename-add-to-basket-button.patch` | 1. Rename a button | `Add to Basket` becomes `Add to Cart` |
| `02-login-form-layout.patch` | 2. Change the structure of a form | The login form gets a new field label and a new order of its parts |
| `03-move-coupon-to-basket.patch` | 3. Move a step of the checkout | The coupon panel moves from `My Payment Options` to the basket page |
| `04-rename-place-order-button.patch` | 1. Rename a button | `Place your order and pay` becomes `Confirm and pay` |

## 01: rename the button `Add to Basket`

Kind: 1, rename a button.

File: `frontend/src/assets/i18n/en.json`, key `ADD_BASKET`.

What changes for a user:

- On each product card in the product list `/#/search`, the button shows `Add to Cart`. Before the change, it showed `Add to Basket`.
- The button has the same position, the same icon and the same function.
- The message after the click does not change: `Placed <product> into basket.`
- The top bar button `Your Basket` does not change.

Test case steps that the change touches:

| Test case | Step | How a person does the step after the change |
|---|---|---|
| TC-02 | 1 | The product card shows the name, the price `8.99¤` and the button `Add to Cart`. |
| TC-02 | 2 | Click `Add to Cart` on the product. |
| TC-04 | 1, 5 | Click `Add to Cart` on the product. |
| TC-07 | 1 | Click `Add to Cart` on product A two times and on product B one time. |

## 02: change the structure of the login form

Kind: 2, change the structure of a form.

Files: `frontend/src/app/login/login.component.html`, `frontend/src/app/login/login.component.scss`, `frontend/src/assets/i18n/en.json` (new key `LABEL_EMAIL_ADDRESS`).

What changes for a user on the login page `/#/login`:

- The label of the email field is `Email address`. Before the change, it was `Email`.
- The checkbox `Remember me` moves up. It is now below the field `Password` and above the button `Log in`. Before the change, it was below the button.
- The link `Forgot your password?` moves down. It is now below the button `Log in`, in the center. Before the change, it was below the field `Password`.
- The title `Login`, the field `Password`, the button `Log in` and the error `Invalid email or password.` do not change.
- The registration page and the page "forgot password" keep the label `Email`.

Test case steps that the change touches:

| Test case | Step | How a person does the step after the change |
|---|---|---|
| TC-01 | 1 | The page shows the title `Login`, the fields `Email address` and `Password`, and the button `Log in`. |
| TC-01 | 2, 4 | Type the email in the field `Email address`. Type the password in the field `Password`. Click `Log in`. The checkbox `Remember me` is now between the field `Password` and the button `Log in`. Do not click it. |

The login of the other test cases (TC-02 to TC-08, precondition "the customer is logged in") also uses this form if a person logs in through the UI.

## 03: move the coupon to the basket page

Kind: 3, move a step of the checkout.

Files: `frontend/src/app/basket/basket.component.html`, `.ts`, `.scss`, `frontend/src/app/payment/payment.component.html`, `.ts`.

What changes for a user:

- The basket page `/#/basket` shows the panel `Add a coupon`. The panel is below the product list and above the button `Checkout`.
- The page `My Payment Options` does not show the panel `Add a coupon`. The page still shows the saved cards, `Wallet Balance`, the button `Pay <total>¤` and the panel `Other payment options`.
- The panel holds the same parts as before: the field `Coupon`, the button `Redeem` and the same messages.
- The coupon logic does not change. It is the same code and calls the same API. The discount, the message `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.` and the error `Invalid coupon.` do not change.
- The basket line `Total Price` shows the price without the discount, as before. The order summary shows the line `Promotion` and the discounted `Total Price`, as before. The button `Pay <total>¤` on the page `My Payment Options` includes the discount, as before.

Test case steps that the change touches:

| Test case | Step | How a person does the step after the change |
|---|---|---|
| TC-05 | 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the coupon code in the field `Coupon`. Click `Redeem`. The basket shows `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.` Then click `Checkout`. The page `Select an address` shows the saved address. |
| TC-05 | 2 | No change. |
| TC-05 | 3 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. The page `My Payment Options` shows the saved card. It does not show the panel `Add a coupon`. |
| TC-05 | 4 | The person did this step in the basket, before the click on `Checkout` (see step 1). |
| TC-05 | 5 | No change. The page `Order Summary` shows `Items` `17.98¤`, `Delivery` `0.99¤`, `Promotion` `1.80¤` and `Total Price` `17.17¤`. |
| TC-06 | 1 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Do steps 3 and 4 here: type the invalid code, click `Redeem`, read the error `Invalid coupon.`. Then type the expired coupon, click `Redeem`, read the error `Invalid coupon.`. Then click `Checkout`, select the saved address and click `Continue`. |
| TC-06 | 2 | No change. The page `My Payment Options` opens, without the panel `Add a coupon`. |
| TC-06 | 3, 4 | The person did these steps in the basket (see step 1). |
| TC-06 | 5 | No change. `Promotion` is `0.00¤` and `Total Price` is `18.97¤`. |
| TC-07 | 2 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. Do step 5 here: open the panel `Add a coupon`, type the coupon code, click `Redeem`, read `Your discount of 10% will be applied during checkout.`. |
| TC-07 | 3, 4 | No change. Click `Checkout` in the basket. |
| TC-07 | 5 | The person did this step in the basket (see step 2). |
| TC-07 | 6 | No change. `Promotion` is `2.10¤` and `Total Price` is `19.86¤`. |

TC-08 does not use a coupon. Its steps on the page `My Payment Options` (`Wallet Balance`, the button `Pay 8.99¤`) do not change.

## 04: rename the button `Place your order and pay`

Kind: 1, rename a button.

File: `frontend/src/assets/i18n/en.json`, key `PLACE_ORDER_AND_PAY`.

What changes for a user:

- On the page `Order Summary`, the button shows `Confirm and pay`. Before the change, it showed `Place your order and pay`.
- The button has the same position and the same function. The confirmation page `Thank you for your purchase!` does not change.

Test case steps that the change touches:

| Test case | Step | How a person does the step after the change |
|---|---|---|
| TC-07 | 7 | Click `Confirm and pay`. The confirmation page `/#/order-completion/<order ID>` shows `Thank you for your purchase!` |
| TC-08 | 8 | Click `Confirm and pay`. The confirmation page shows `Thank you for your purchase!` |

## All patches together

With all 4 patches, each change in the sections 01 to 04 applies. The changes do not have an effect on each other.
In TC-07, for example, a person clicks `Add to Cart` (01), logs in with the field `Email address` (02), redeems the coupon in the basket (03) and clicks `Confirm and pay` (04).

Steps that no patch touches: TC-01 steps 3 and 5, TC-02 steps 3 and 4, TC-03 all steps, TC-04 steps 2 to 4, TC-07 steps 8 to 10, TC-08 steps 1 to 7 and 9 to 10.

## Results of the checks

### `git apply --check`, each patch alone on v20.3.0

Command: `git -C ../juice-shop apply --check ../sealed-ui/<file>.patch`. Before each command, `../juice-shop` was at the tag v20.3.0 with no changes.

```
01 alone: exit 0
02 alone: exit 0
03 alone: exit 0
04 alone: exit 0
```

### All patches together, in file-name order

For each patch in the order 01, 02, 03, 04: `git apply --check`, then `git apply`, on top of the patches before it.

```
01: check exit 0, applied
02 on top of 01: check exit 0, applied
03 on top of 01-02: check exit 0, applied
04 on top of 01-03: check exit 0, applied
```

`git -C ../juice-shop status --porcelain` after all 4 patches:

```
 M frontend/src/app/basket/basket.component.html
 M frontend/src/app/basket/basket.component.scss
 M frontend/src/app/basket/basket.component.ts
 M frontend/src/app/login/login.component.html
 M frontend/src/app/login/login.component.scss
 M frontend/src/app/payment/payment.component.html
 M frontend/src/app/payment/payment.component.ts
 M frontend/src/assets/i18n/en.json
```

### Build with all patches

Command, in `../juice-shop/frontend`:

```
npx ng build --configuration production --output-path "$TMPDIR/ui-patch-build"
```

Result: the build passed, with no errors and no warnings in the output. Last lines of the output:

```
Application bundle generation complete. [11.283 seconds] - 2026-10-21T16:08:32.431Z

Output location: /var/folders/8v/tjlqcph57g934z54rbf7jfk40000gn/T/ui-patch-build
```

The build did not write into `../juice-shop/frontend/dist`. The app was not started.

### Reset of the app

After the build: `git -C ../juice-shop checkout -- .`.
Then `git -C ../juice-shop status --porcelain` gave no output, and `git -C ../juice-shop describe --tags --exact-match HEAD` gave `v20.3.0`.

## Limits

- Nobody did the steps of TC-01 to TC-08 in a browser with the patches. The analysis of the steps above comes from the source code. The build shows only that the code compiles.
- The unit tests of the frontend were not run or read. The task did not permit it. The unit tests of the basket, payment and login components can fail with patches 02 and 03.
